Distribution and Ecology. The range of the new species is restricted to the central and southern parts of the Zagros mountains in Iran (Fig. 5). Adults fly very late in the season, usually in xerophytic habitats with thorny Astragalus and Acantholimon, and nectar on flowers of Acantholimon and Acanthophyllum. They are petrophilous and generally prefer to stay near the ground and rocks where the patterns on the underside of their hindwings provide an adaptive camouflage against predators. They can also be seen resting on the tree trunks in cool shady spots.
